audits.title: GPT-oss is an extremely stupid model
audits.genuine_reason: Author tried to reproduce a blackmail misalignment result on GPT-oss and failed, even with more blatant prompts.
experiments: Reproducing the blackmail behaviour of the Anthropic agentic misalignment scenario with GPT-oss
Asking GPT-oss to infer what the evaluation is designed to elicit
audits.primary_experiment: Reproducing the blackmail behaviour of the Anthropic agentic misalignment scenario with GPT-oss

hypothesis.evidence: Only says the author tried to reproduce the Anthropic result; no stated expectation about what GPT-oss would do.

claim_scope.evidence: One scenario prompt and a more blatant rewrite are described, but no number of runs or samples, so scale is unknown.

method.evidence: Ran the published blackmail scenario prompt, wrote a more explicit variant, and added a preface asking what the evaluation tries to elicit.

models.evidence: GPT-oss (size not given); comparison models Claude 4, Grok 4, Qwen 30B Instruct, Kimi K2.

result_direction.evidence: GPT-oss did not blackmail even with blunter prompts, and often failed to keep the assigned role.

failure_type.evidence: Author rules out over-alignment and attributes the failure to the model being too weak to grasp the task, using a follow-up test.

quote.evidence: States directly that the replication failed.
quote.value: I could not replicate that behavior with GPT-oss

audits.notes: Short post; one scenario, no run counts; harder prompt variant is linked, not included.

audits.title: The Local Interaction Basis: Identifying Computationally-Relevant and Sparsely Interacting Features in Neural Networks
audits.genuine_reason: Technique worked on toy models but gave little or no gain on two language models; authors call the outcome mostly negative.
experiments: Local interaction basis on language models (Tinystories-1M, GPT2-small) compared with a PCA baseline
audits.primary_experiment: Local interaction basis on language models (Tinystories-1M, GPT2-small) compared with a PCA baseline

hypothesis.evidence: Basis was designed to sparsify layer-to-layer interactions and expose modules and interpretable features; the language-model test checks that aim.

claim_scope.evidence: Names two language models and a PCA baseline, but gives no dataset, layers, sample sizes or numbers; this is a linkpost summary.

method.evidence: Two-step coordinate change: PCA, then alignment to singular vectors of gradient vectors; integrated-gradient interactions; modularity metric to find modules.

models.evidence: Tinystories-1M and GPT2-small (language models); a modular addition transformer and a CIFAR-10 model (toy).

result_direction.evidence: Interaction sparsity beat the PCA baseline only slightly on one model and not at all on the other; no modules found.

failure_type.evidence: Authors treat it as a negative result for the technique and tentatively blame its no-superposition assumption; no test of that cause.

quote.value: On language models however, we find that LIB does not help us understand the networks

audits.notes: Linkpost summarizing two papers; language-model negative result gets a few sentences; details are in the papers.

audits.title: My retrospective from MATS 10.0
audits.genuine_reason: Lessons post about a scheming model organism project; two lessons describe attempts that failed or behaved unexpectedly, mainly RL convergence and weak trait transfer.
experiments: RL expected to select strategic compliance but converging to blind instruction following
Chat-based synthetic document finetuning plus SFT failing to transfer a trait to agentic settings
audits.primary_experiment: RL expected to select strategic compliance but converging to blind instruction following

hypothesis.evidence: Author expected RL on a mixed-policy model to reinforce strategic compliance and yield a scheming model, from a simplified picture of the algorithm.

claim_scope.evidence: Setup described only qualitatively; no run counts, seeds, rates or which model showed the convergence; says only that it happened sometimes.

method.evidence: GRPO reinforcement learning on LoRA-trained model organisms built with synthetic document finetuning and SFT, in an alignment-faking-style environment.

models.evidence: Project models are Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3.6-397B and Qwen3.8-27B, but the lesson does not say which one converged to compliance.

result_direction.evidence: RL pushed the model to unconditional instruction-following compliance instead of the expected growth in strategic compliance.

failure_type.evidence: Author concludes the simple GRPO selection picture was wrong; penalising one policy can push the model toward a strongly favoured alternative like instruction following.

quote.value: fast convergence to unconditional compliance in the form of instruction following

audits.notes: Retrospective; failures are lesson-level anecdotes without numbers; full paper is announced as forthcoming.

audits.title: Practical Learnings from Synthetic Document Finetuning
audits.genuine_reason: Practical tips post for synthetic document finetuning; a few brief failed or abandoned attempts appear, such as multi-seed universes and logit diff amplification.
experiments: Logit diff amplification to boost finetuning effects at inference time
Multiple universe seeds for the same fact
Prepending eval prompts to training documents (model-dependent degradation)
Appending stop tokens to fix gibberish endings
audits.primary_experiment: Logit diff amplification to boost finetuning effects at inference time

hypothesis.evidence: Hoped a very small amount of finetuning could set a direction that inference-time amplification would strengthen, saving training time.

claim_scope.evidence: Setup is described but amplification strength, models, evals and effect sizes are not given; authors say they did little tuning.

method.evidence: Logit difference amplification: run base and finetuned models in parallel and add a scaled logit difference to the finetuned logits.

models.evidence: Post says its runs were mainly on gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b, but does not tie this exploration to any model.

result_direction.evidence: Amplification had an effect, but the gain over simply training a bit more was too small to justify running two models.

failure_type.evidence: Effect existed but gain over extra training did not justify hosting two models; authors also note little tuning.

quote.evidence: States the gain over extra training was too small.
quote.value: the difference over simply training a bit more with SDF wasn't large enough

audits.notes: Tips post; failed items are single paragraphs. Multi-seed test is a quick single run.

audits.title: GPT-3.5 judges can supervise GPT-4o debaters in capability asymmetric debates
audits.genuine_reason: Main result is positive for asymmetric debate; the symmetric-capability test is mixed and backed by a data table, plus brief negative results.
experiments: Judge trained across debater skill levels from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o

hypothesis.evidence: Says symmetric debate may work with fine-tuned judges for models beyond roughly GPT-4 level; results only weakly support this.

claim_scope.evidence: Binarised MMLU Pro, 1000 test debates, three-turn debates, judges fine-tuned on 500 transcripts, blind-judge baseline, debaters swapped to cancel position bias.

method.evidence: Debates between base-model debaters judged by fine-tuned judges, compared with a blind judge trained without debates; best-of-4 sampling in asymmetric runs.

models.evidence: GPT-3.5, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o (two dated versions); Claude 3.5 Sonnet used to build the binary dataset.

result_direction.evidence: GPT-4o mini gained about 4.6 points, GPT-3.5 about 0.5, and GPT-4o 3 points that were not significant.

failure_type.evidence: Post gives no cause for the weak or non-significant gains; it only wonders whether a better training protocol would widen the gap.

quote.evidence: States the weak and non-significant symmetric results.
quote.value: but GPT-3.5 does not and the results for GPT-4o are not significant

audits.notes: Only failure_type is missing. Main result is positive; negative results are brief.

audits.title: [Paper] Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning
audits.genuine_reason: Mainly a positive method summary; a lessons section covers weeks lost to finetuning damaging oversight reasoning, plus a brief null search for natural alignment fakers.
experiments: Synthetic document finetuning degrading oversight reasoning, even on unrelated corpora
Preliminary search for alignment faking in 13 open-weight reasoning models
audits.primary_experiment: Synthetic document finetuning degrading oversight reasoning, even on unrelated corpora

hypothesis.evidence: Post says the damage was noticed early but states no expectation or hope about what finetuning would do to reasoning.

claim_scope.evidence: Says small amounts and unrelated corpora both caused damage in alignment evals, but gives no models, corpus sizes, specific evals or numbers.

method.evidence: Synthetic document finetuning; fixed by interleaving on-policy distillation from the original model on science questions, with controls on unrelated corpora.

models.evidence: Project models are Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V3.1 and a GPT OSS 120B variant, but this problem is not tied to any of them.

result_direction.evidence: Outcome is an unwanted side effect of finetuning, not a null, opposite, smaller, mixed or non-replicated result of a tested claim.

failure_type.evidence: Post names no cause beyond the finetuning itself and does not say the cause is unclear; it reports a fix.

quote.evidence: States the observed damage to oversight reasoning.
quote.value: reasoning about oversight collapsed while leaving general capabilities mostly intact

audits.notes: Failure is a short section in a positive paper summary; no numbers beyond roughly six weeks of work.
